sections.name: architecture
sections.value: Auth is already two-phase (`auth::stage` → `StagedAuth::publish`) and `boot::serve` binds before publishing, with a comment stating the invariant. The observed clobber therefore comes from a path that does not honour it (the --json/sandbox boot at boot.rs:207-224 stages into a directory that may resolve to the global config dir; or a staged NamedTempFile promoted on an error path; or a bind on a different address family succeeding). t1 finds it by test, t2 closes it structurally: publish is only reachable from a bound listener (make publish take the bound listener, or a proof token from bind). The 401 hint gets an mtime-vs-boot check. A prod-owner designation (env or config) refuses the prod database from foreign cwds — the cheapest defence against another government's default-config daemon.

value.rationale: One unit, one coder, no PM; o-prime coordinates directly (Jordan, 2026-09-02: dispatch the performance work to agents).

value.name: daemon-key-after-bind
value.paths: crates/daemon/src/auth.rs; crates/daemon/src/boot.rs; crates/daemon/src/http.rs (401 body only); crates/cli/src/** (401 rendering + hint); crates/core/src/config.rs (owner designation); crates/daemon/tests/**; crates/cli/tests/**; docs/plans/017-daemon-key-after-bind/**
value.responsibility: reproduce the shared-key clobber; make key publication impossible without a bound listener on every boot path; honest 401 hint; prod-database owner designation; test-setup transcript
value.interface: `StagedAuth::publish` becomes reachable only with a bound listener (signature change internal to fs3-daemon); 401 envelope gains `key_newer_than_daemon: bool` and a corrected `fix`; config gains an owner designation (env FS3_PROD_OWNER=1 or [daemon].owner_root); daemon refuses the prod database from foreign cwds with FS3-E-PROD-NOT-DESIGNATED. Additive envelope changes only.
value.test_strategy: two-daemon integration test (A listening, B same config, normal and --json) asserting key bytes/mtime + no temp file + A's clients OK; boot-sequence unit test with a pre-bound port; CLI 401 render test; config/boot designation tests; one mutation receipt per rule; test-setup transcript
value.note: NEVER run a daemon with the default config: every test daemon uses FS3_CONFIG_DIR=<scratch>, the :5434 database and an ephemeral port. Prod :7373/:5433 and ~/.config/flowspace3 are never touched (that is the incident this packet fixes).
Your worktree is fs3-daemon-key-after-bind on branch 017-daemon-key-after-bind. Scratch config dirs only; :5434 only; ephemeral ports only.

value.steps: None — single unit. o-prime squash-merges and bounces prod (daemon/store binary changes).
value.integration_proof: the real-usage criteria in the plan, measured on prod after the bounce

value.when: spawned by o-prime once the PR is up
value.inputs: t1 must name the real writing path with a red test on main, not a guess; publish unreachable without a bound listener on EVERY path incl. --json/sandbox; the 401 hint's mtime check cannot false-positive on a normal restart (key mtime == boot); designation refuses by cwd AND accepts by env/config; error text names the test URL; the transcript is reproducible on the test setup

value.text: the clobber path may be the --json sandbox boot writing into the global dir when FS3_CONFIG_DIR is unset — t1 decides; do not fix before reproducing
the owner designation must not break o-prime's own bounce from the main clone (cwd inside the root) or `bin/daemon-restart`
the 401 hint reads the daemon's boot time — expose it on /health or in the 401 body rather than guessing from the pid
